title: Targeting Tat-TAR RNA Interaction for HIV-1 Inhibition.
authors: Alanazi, Awadh; Ivanov, Andrey; Kumari, Namita; Lin, Xionghao; Wang, Songping; Kovalskyy, Dmytro; Nekhai, Sergei
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接筛选靶向Tat-TAR RNA互作的小分子抑制剂，虽涉及RNA-蛋白互作建模，但对象为RNA而非DNA，且无TF-DNA结合机制研究，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: The HIV-1 Tat protein interacts with TAR RNA and recruits CDK9/cyclin T1 and other host factors to induce HIV-1 transcription. Thus, Tat-TAR RNA interaction, which is unique for HIV-1, represents an attractive target for anti-HIV-1 therapeutics. To target Tat-TAR RNA interaction, we used a crystal structure of acetylpromazine bound to the bulge of TAR RNA, to dock compounds from the Enamine database containing over two million individual compounds. The docking procedure identified 173 compounds that were further analyzed for the inhibition of HIV-1 infection. The top ten inhibitory compounds with IC(50) </= 6 microM were selected and the three least toxic compounds, T6780107 (IC(50) = 2.97 muM), T0516-4834 (IC(50) = 0.2 muM) and T5628834 (IC(50) = 3.46 muM), were further tested for HIV-1 transcription inhibition. Only the T0516-4834 compound showed selective inhibition of Tat-induced HIV-1 transcription, whereas the T6780107 compound inhibited equally basal and Tat-induced transcription and the T5628834 compound only inhibited basal HIV-1 transcription. The compounds were tested for the inhibition of translation and showed minimal (<25%) effect. The T0516-4834 compound also showed the strongest inhibition of HIV-1 RNA expression and p24 production in CEM T cells and peripheral blood mononuclear cells infected with HIV-1 IIIB. Of the three compounds, only the T0516-4834 compound significantly disrupted Tat-TAR RNA interaction. Additionally, of the three tested compounds, T5628834 and, to a lesser extent, T0516-4834 disrupted Tat-CDK9/cyclin T1 interaction. None of the three compounds showed significant inhibition of the cellular CDK9 and cyclin T1 levels. In silico modelling showed that the T0516-4834 compound interacted with TAR RNA by binding to the bulge formed by U23, U25, C39, G26,C39 and U40 residues. Taken together, our study identified a novel benzoxazole compound that disrupted Tat-TAR RNA interaction and inhibited Tat-induced transcription and HIV-1 infection, suggesting that this compound might serve as a new lead for anti-HIV-1 therapeutics.
abstract_zh: HIV-1 Tat蛋白与TAR RNA相互作用，并招募CDK9/cyclin T1及其他宿主因子以诱导HIV-1转录。因此，Tat-TAR RNA相互作用是HIV-1特有的，代表了抗HIV-1治疗的一个有吸引力的靶点。为靶向Tat-TAR RNA相互作用，我们利用乙酰丙嗪与TAR RNA凸起结合的晶体结构，对Enamine数据库中超过两百万个化合物的结构进行对接。对接过程鉴定出173种化合物，并进一步分析其对HIV-1感染的抑制作用。选择IC(50) ≤ 6 μM的十种最佳抑制化合物，并进一步测试其中三种毒性最低的化合物T6780107（IC(50) = 2.97 μM）、T0516-4834（IC(50) = 0.2 μM）和T5628834（IC(50) = 3.46 μM）对HIV-1转录的抑制作用。仅T0516-4834化合物显示出对Tat诱导的HIV-1转录的选择性抑制，而T6780107化合物对基础和Tat诱导的转录均有同等抑制，T5628834化合物仅抑制基础HIV-1转录。这些化合物在翻译抑制测试中显示出最小（<25%）效应。T0516-4834化合物在感染HIV-1 IIIB的CEM T细胞和外周血单核细胞中也显示出最强的HIV-1 RNA表达和p24产生抑制作用。在这三种化合物中，仅T0516-4834显著破坏Tat-TAR RNA相互作用。此外，在测试的三种化合物中，T5628834以及较小程度的T0516-4834破坏了Tat-CDK9/cyclin T1相互作用。三种化合物均未显著抑制细胞CDK9和cyclin T1水平。计算机模拟显示，T0516-4834化合物通过与U23、U25、C39、G26、C39和U40残基形成的凸起结合来与TAR RNA相互作用。综合来看，我们的研究鉴定了一种新型苯并噁唑化合物，该化合物破坏了Tat-TAR RNA相互作用并抑制Tat诱导的转录和HIV-1感染，表明该化合物可能作为抗HIV-1治疗的新先导物。
